the biosynthesis of the CO and CN ligands for the [FeFe]-hydrogenase active sites.
the mechanism of CN−/CO biosynthesis and the role of the HydG protein in this process.
the biosynthesis of the active site of [FeFe]-hydrogenases by the maturase HydE and HydG.

HydG uses a glycyl free radical to synthesize the [FeFe]-hydrogenase active-site ligands.
the HydG maturase synthesizes CO from a glycyl radical.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthesis of CN−/CO by HydG occurs in two domains and that the synthesis of the CN−/H2CNH fragment is initiated by a free radical.
HydG uses a glycyl free radical for CN− synthesis and a [4Fe–S] cluster for CO synthesis.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a glycyl free radical is the initial precursor in the synthesis by HydG of the [FeFe]-hydrogenase active-site ligands, CO and CN−.
